subject: Post-call recap: PilotPay discovery — cost drivers, levers & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@pilotpay.com>; Kira Matsui <kira.m@pilotpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: PilotPay discovery — cost drivers, levers & next steps

Alex / Kira — thanks again for the 30-minute sync today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Key pain points you called out
- High token spend due to long user prompts + multi-turn context in support flows (~1.3k avg tokens per session).
- Peak latency constraints for live support (p95 target <= 350ms).
- Tight pilot budget: procurement indicated ~ $60k–$90k/mo cap for initial pilot.

Goals we captured
1) Validate semantic routing for triage (reduce human-handled tickets by 15–20%).
2) Verify latency/quality on 1M monthly requests projected after onboarding.
3) Prove a 30–40% unit-cost reduction vs current managed endpoint using batching + caching.

Cost / TCO assumptions we used in the call (prelim)
- Monthly query volume: 1,000,000 requests
- Avg tokens/request: 1,300 input + 120 output = ~1,420 tokens
- Baseline (no batching, hosted model A): estimated unit cost X -> ~$150k/mo (rough)
- With caching + conservative batching + quantized model variant: estimated range $70k–$95k/mo (pilot scope).

Levers we recommended and short tradeoffs
- Batching (continuous micro-batching): reduces per-token GPU amortization; helps with cost but must be tuned for p95 latency.
- Prefix/KV caching: very high impact for repeated prompts (support templates); strong win if 30–40% of requests share prefixes.
- Quantized model variant (8-bit): ~15–25% lower GPU cost, slight quality delta to validate in eval set.
- Dedicated pool / commitment: if committing to reserved capacity for production, we can shape a cheaper sustained rate.

Pilot proposal (next 60 days) — minimal viable scope
- 2-week ingest of request traces (we'll use the attached sample traces as a template).
- 4-week pilot: host two model variants (quantized + baseline) behind routing with caching on high-frequency prefixes.
- Ops: Redwood will run the pilot; require one infra contact (Kira) and access window for request traces.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Alex / Kira: confirm that sharing 2 weeks of traces is OK (S3 presigned link or secure Drive).
- Procurement: rough budget gate of $75k/mo will determine pilot sizing — please confirm target number.
- Schedule: propose a 30-min technical kickoff next Wed 3/16 — is 10:00am PT OK?

Attachments included: pilot-scope-estimate.xlsx (cost scenarios), sample-request-traces.jsonl (format), redwood-batching-single-sheet.pdf (one-pager).

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for a short technical pre-read. If anything above is off, call it out and I'll update.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
"Make inference predictable and economical for every engineering team."

From: Alex Russo <alex.russo@pilotpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kira Matsui <kira.m@pilotpay.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 16:03:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: PilotPay discovery — cost drivers, levers & next steps

Thanks Dylan — this is a great recap and aligns with our notes. A few quick clarifications: 

- Budget: procurement surfaced a hard stop at $75k/mo for the pilot window unless we can show definitive cost offsets by week 3.
- Traces: we can share two weeks of anonymized traces. Kira will put together an S3 presigned link by EOD tomorrow.
- Latency: the 350ms p95 is firm for customer-facing triage; internal agent flows can tolerate up to 800ms p95. That matters for batching choices.

A couple asks from our side:
- Can you include a simple per-10k-requests delta table for the two model variants (baseline vs quantized) so our finance team can see marginal impact?
- We will want a short statement on data retention and where logs live during the pilot for our security review.

Happy to join the kickoff next Wed 3/16 at 10:00am PT — Kira will confirm.

Alex
Alex Russo
Head of Product, PilotPay
alex.russo@pilotpay.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@pilotpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: PilotPay discovery — cost drivers, levers & next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick notes and the budget clarity. Actionables on our side before the kickoff:
- I'll attach a short delta table (per-10k-requests) and an updated cost-scenarios sheet (see pilot-scope-estimate.xlsx) — Karthik will validate the math.
- Marissa will add a two-paragraph data-retention note for your security team (where logs live, retention window, and how we anonymize traces).
- Kira: once we get the S3 link we'll ingest the 2-week sample and validate cache-hit opportunity within 48 hours.

Proposed next meeting: Wed, 16 Mar 2027, 10:00am PT — invite will go out after Kira confirms.

Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

Dylan

Attachments (referenced) are included in this thread as stubs: pilot-scope-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample-request-traces.jsonl (jsonl), redwood-batching-single-sheet.pdf (pdf).
